description: Add constituency field to User model and create database migration script. The User model in backend/app/models.py currently lacks a constituency column, which is required for constituency-scoped reviewer dashboards. Add a nullable String constituency column to the User model using SQLAlchemy Mapped annotations (matching the pattern in the existing model). Create a standalone migration script at backend/add_user_constituency.py that adds the column to existing databases using ALTER TABLE, following SQLite and PostgreSQL syntax patterns.
steps: Add 'constituency: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100), nullable=True, default=None)' to the User class in backend/app/models.py, after the 'role' field

Create backend/add_user_constituency.py migration script that: imports sqlalchemy and database engine from app.database, uses raw SQL 'ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN constituency VARCHAR(100)' with try/except to handle column-already-exists error, prints success/skip message
Update the StaffUserIn schema in backend/app/schemas.py to add optional 'constituency: str = ""' field
Update the UserOut schema in backend/app/schemas.py to include 'constituency: str' field so API responses expose the new column
Modify POST /api/admin/users endpoint in backend/app/main.py to read data.constituency from StaffUserIn and set it on the staff_user object during creation
Add audit log entry in POST /api/admin/users that includes the constituency value in the details parameter when a staff user is created with a constituency assignment
acceptance_criteria: User model has constituency column defined with nullable String(100) type
Migration script backend/add_user_constituency.py exists and can be run with 'cd backend && python add_user_constituency.py' without error
Running migration script on existing database adds the column; running it again prints 'Column already exists' without error
StaffUserIn schema accepts constituency field in POST /api/admin/users payload
UserOut schema returns constituency field in GET /api/auth/me response
Creating a staff user via POST /api/admin/users with constituency value stores and returns that value
verification: Start backend server: cd backend && uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
Run migration script: cd backend && python add_user_constituency.py (should print success)
Run migration script again: cd backend && python add_user_constituency.py (should print already exists)
Test API manually: POST /api/admin/users with admin token, include 'constituency' in payload, verify response includes the constituency value
Test API manually: GET /api/auth/me as that created user, verify constituency appears in response
